findings.description: publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL endpoint a public IP, exposing the database to the internet in combination with a security group that accepts traffic from a routable range.
storage_encrypted = false leaves the catalog database, its snapshots, and read replicas unencrypted, so data is readable in cleartext from the underlying storage.

The user_data script writes the RDS master password from var.password, along with the DB username and endpoint, into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc in cleartext. User data is retrievable from the instance metadata service and the file persists on the instance filesystem, so the DB credential is exposed to anyone with shell or metadata access and is baked into Terraform state.

The role assumed by the EC2 instance grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", giving any code on the app server full control of storage, compute, and databases, including privilege escalation and mass data destruction if the instance is compromised.
The database security group permits all outbound traffic (protocol -1, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, enabling unrestricted outbound connections and data exfiltration from the database tier.
MySQL 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR rather than to the application security group, so any host in the VPC can reach the database rather than only the intended application tier.
The instance is created with the well-known master username "admin", which lowers the effort required to guess valid credentials for an internet-reachable database.
The application connects to MySQL without TLS enforcement and the DB name, username, and password are stored in a plaintext include file, so credentials and data can be transmitted in cleartext.

findings.issue_category: database subnet group in public subnets
findings.description: The DB subnet group is composed of the portal subnets used by the publicly reachable application server, so the RDS instance is placed in subnets that may route to the internet, reinforcing the publicly_accessible exposure.
